title: A choice for each value
idea: Combine for-item-in-list with an if inside the body, so the action depends on each value. Reviews if inside a loop.

exercises.explanation: The if runs each pass. 80 and 55 are >= 50 so 'pass' prints twice; 40 is below, so it's skipped.

exercises.prompt: Putting an if inside a for-each loop lets the action depend on the current value.
exercises.explanation: Each pass the if checks the current value and decides whether to do the action. Same if you learned earlier, now per item.
Only values greater than 5 are printed: 8 and 10 qualify; 3 and 1 don't.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the code: for each temperature, print 'hot' only if it is above 30.
exercises.explanation: List, then loop header, then the if (indented once), then its body (indented twice). 35 prints 'hot'; 25 doesn't.
An even number has remainder 0 when divided by 2, so the test is n % 2 == 0.

options: Four — one per item (adult or minor)
exercises.explanation: With if/else, every pass prints exactly one line. Four items means four lines: minor, adult, minor, adult.

options: Once to be inside the loop, again to be inside the if
exercises.explanation: Each level of 'inside' adds indentation: inside the loop, then inside the if. The print belongs to both.

exercises.prompt: The if is checked fresh on every pass, using whatever value the loop variable holds that time.
exercises.explanation: Yes — the condition is re-evaluated each pass with the current value, so different items can take different branches.
Only 50 is above 40, so only its labelled line prints.

exercises.prompt: You want to print only the items in [7, 2, 9, 4] that are below 5. Which test goes in the if?
